consensus_summary: Sand primarily symbolizes an innumerable multitude (Abrahamic promise, vast peoples/armies: Gen 22:17; Hos 1:10; Rev 20:8), with a widely taught secondary meaning of unstable/foolish foundation from Matthew 7:26-27, plus minor senses (divine boundary of the sea, heaviness/burden).
book_summary: Sand is a countless multitude; and when used as a foundation (Matt 7:26) it signifies the instability of building upon the crowd — people not bound together by a covenant — as opposed to the covenant Rock.
consensus_core_identification: Innumerable multitude (primary), with a distinct, unrelated secondary sense of unstable foundation in Matthew 7.
book_core_identification: Innumerable multitude, with the Matthew 7 sand-foundation specifically identified as that same multitude — the uncovenanted crowd — making instability a function of building on the crowd rather than the covenant Rock.
boundary_disagreement: The consensus treats the multitude sense and the unstable-foundation sense as two independent, passage-specific meanings that 'coexist without conflict.' The book unifies them: the sand of Matthew 7 is not generic instability but the multitude itself considered as a foundation — the crowd lacking covenant bonds. This reclassifies the Matthew 7 case from a separate metaphor into a specification of the multitude symbol, and adds the covenant/Rock opposition as a defining condition.
rationale: The book's central identification (countless multitude) is equivalent to the consensus primary, and the instability sense it includes corresponds to the consensus's most common alternative. However, the book materially changes the precision and grounds of the Matthew 7 reading: instability is redefined as building on the uncovenanted crowd, tying the two consensus meanings into one symbol with an explicit Rock opposite. This is a genuine boundary/precision change within the same referent category, not a replacement of the consensus identification, so REFINED rather than MATCH or DIVERGENT.
strongest_objection: One could argue MATCH: the book simply lists both consensus meanings (multitude and unstable foundation), and the 'crowd not bound by covenant' phrasing is interpretive gloss rather than a material change in extension — the same passages are covered with the same practical import.
